name: Acoustic Marrow Shear Rifle AMSR-6 'Tutor'
description:
The Acoustic Marrow Shear Rifle operates on a principle of targeted endoskeletal resonance: it generates a highly focused ultrasonic beam tuned to the specific resonant frequency of cortical bone, which — when sustained for more than 0.4 seconds on a single point — induces shear fractures propagating outward from the beam's entry point through the target's skeletal structure. The AMSR-6 does not break bones by impact; it teaches bones to break themselves. The beam passes through soft tissue with minimal interaction, causing no surface wound, no visible entry point, no blood. The damage is entirely internal, distributed along stress lines that the resonance calculates in real time through a return-echo analysis system built into the barrel.

RINGO CORPONATION developed the AMSR-6 under a research grant nominally aimed at non-invasive orthopedic correction technology. The weaponization of the platform was, according to public records, an unforeseen application. Internal documents that surfaced during a RINGO lawsuit tell a different story. The AMSR-6's return-echo analysis — which maps a target's skeletal structure before inducing shear — gives the weapon an unusual precision: operators can select which bones to fracture, at what severity, and in what sequence. Field manuals for licensed users include targeting protocols with names like 'immobilize,' 'incapacitate,' and 'structural cascade,' the last of which involves inducing simultaneous fractures across load-bearing skeletal points.

The weapon's street name 'Tutor' comes from the way victims describe surviving a partial engagement: 'It taught me something about my own body I didn't want to know.' The AMSR-6 is long-barreled, requiring a bipod for stable operation, and its discharge is below the threshold of human hearing — operators sometimes describe it as 'the loudest silent thing they've ever used,' because the moment of discharge is marked only by the target's reaction. At distance, victims appear to simply crumple. There is no muzzle flash. There is no sound.
tier_availability: Tier 4+; black market availability is growing
legality: Restricted — classified as a precision incapacitation system; 'structural cascade' targeting protocol prohibited under GLMZ Humane Engagement Code
specifications:
effective range: 8–220 meters
beam frequency: Dynamically tuned 18–28 kHz based on echo mapping
mapping time: 0.2 seconds per target before first engagement
minimum engagement duration: 0.4 seconds for initial fracture induction
power source: RINGO AcoustiCell pack — 12 full engagements per charge
weight: 5.6 kg with bipod
discharge signature: Sub-audible; no visible emission; no thermal signature
tactical_use: Used by precision operators in surveillance-heavy environments where a shot must be undetectable. Snipers favor it for operations requiring the target to be incapacitated rather than killed — a standing target that crumples without apparent cause takes longer to be identified as a shooting victim, giving the operator extraction time. Military interrogation-adjacent units use the lower intensity settings for coercive compliance. Counter-bodyguard teams use it to disable protection details without alerting the principal.
cultural_context: The AMSR-6 has generated a specific kind of fear in GLMZ that differs from conventional weapon anxiety: it is the fear of invisible, inexplicable harm. Several documented cases of AMSR-6 use in public spaces — where victims collapsed in crowds without apparent cause — have fed an urban legend about 'the bone sickness,' a supposedly environmental hazard in certain districts that causes spontaneous fractures. Public health authorities have periodically issued statements debunking this. The statements are not universally believed. RINGO CORPONATION maintains that the AMSR-6 is used only in authorized contexts and has no comment on specific incidents.
known_users: Black-market operators serving corporate clients who require deniable incapacitation
'The Instructor' — a named but unidentified operator with at least 14 attributed engagements
story_hooks: Three people in different districts have collapsed in public over the past month with unexplained skeletal fractures. The municipal health authority is calling it a structural calcium disorder. A street doctor who treated one of the victims doesn't believe it — the fracture patterns are too precise.

A black-market AMSR-6 is circulating with a modified echo-mapping module that has been updated with a proprietary skeletal database — meaning whoever sold it pre-loaded it with the bone profiles of specific named individuals. The list is still in the firmware.

The Instructor takes a job and then goes silent. Their client wants the job completed. Their former handler wants to know why they stopped. A forensic analyst who's been tracking their work suspects the Instructor is now the target of someone using the same weapon.

RINGO CORPONATION's orthopedic research division files for a patent on 'resonance-assisted fracture correction therapy.' The filing date is three years before the AMSR-6 was supposedly weaponized. Someone has noticed.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, precision instrument resembling a high-end sporting rifle crossed with medical imaging equipment. The silhouette is clean and purposeful—long, slender, almost elegant despite its lethal function. The barrel dominates the profile, appearing almost too thin for a weapon of its class, with subtle ribbed vents running its length. The overall impression is of careful engineering rather than brute force.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 127 cm (with integrated barrel). Barrel length: 71 cm. Width across bipod: 34 cm when deployed. Height at scope rail: 18 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly balanced and light in hand at 5.6 kg—the weight is distributed along the barrel and stock to minimize fatigue during the extended tracking required for return-echo mapping. Not unwieldy; almost delicate by military standards, though the bipod adds substantive heft when deployed.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade titanium alloy frame with carbon-composite barrel housing. The receiver is polished aluminum with precision-machined tolerances visible to the naked eye.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with a subtle brushed texture that minimizes reflection. The barrel housing exhibits a darker, almost black anodized finish that contrasts sharply with the lighter receiver. Wear patterns show as pale scuff marks on high-contact points—bipod mounts, charging mechanism, scope rails.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: gunmetal gray and deep charcoal. Accent: brushed aluminum trim along the scope rail and trigger guard. RINGO corporate blue (RGB: 0, 102, 204) appears as small accent strips near the magazine well and on the AcoustiCell power coupling.
physical_description.grip_texture: Ergonomic polymer grip with fine crosshatch texturing—not aggressive, but precise. The stock is wrapped in thin, matte-finish tactical rubber that absorbs vibration. The trigger guard is bare machined aluminum, cold to the touch.
distinctive_features: Barrel ribbed with acoustic vents—aesthetic but functional, designed to dissipate resonance bleed
Return-echo sensor pod mounted beneath the barrel: a small cylindrical protrusion with faint optical ports
Integrated feedback display in the scope housing—minimal LEDs that glow soft blue during mapping sequence
Magazine well is oversized relative to the rifle's profile, accommodating the AcoustiCell's distinctive cylindrical power pack
No visible muzzle device; the barrel simply terminates in a precision aperture barely 8mm in diameter
Targeting refinement dial on the stock—small rotary mechanism with detent clicks, labeled in frequencies rather than traditional distance markers
Bilateral charging handles recessed into the receiver to prevent snag
Faint RINGO Data Services insignia—a stylized data helix—etched into the upper receiver in silver ink
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: RINGO Data Services logo and model designation 'AMSR-6' stamped in raised text on the left side of the receiver, just above the bipod mount. Serial number engraved on a small titanium plate inset into the stock. 'Property of RINGO Corporation / Licensed Operator Only' etched in fine print along the barrel.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-used specimens show excellent maintenance discipline—carbon scoring around the return-echo sensor pod, minor scratches on the stock from transport in rigid cases, faint salt corrosion on the aluminum trim (indicating use in Great Lakes moisture). Well-maintained examples retain their matte finish integrity; heavily used units develop a patina of fingerprint oils on the grip.

image_prompt: Product photography of the Acoustic Marrow Shear Rifle AMSR-6 'Tutor' laid horizontally on a dark matte black surface, bipod deployed and weapon angled 15 degrees toward camera. Gloved hand (tactical polymer, fingerless) gripping the stock to convey scale. Dramatic side-lighting from upper left, casting sharp shadows from the barrel ribs and return-echo sensor pod, emphasizing the weapon's precision geometry. Cool blue LED glow from the scope display visible in the shadow. Matte gunmetal and charcoal finishes catch light subtly; aluminum accents highlight with surgical brightness. Shallow depth of field: barrel and scope in sharp focus, background dark and diffuse. Cyberpunk aesthetic: sterile, clinical, high-tech. No blood, no destruction—the aesthetic is of clinical precision, not violence. Corporate clean. --ar 3:2 --v 6
